walkthroughs.body_html: Inputs: wave/wind/tide energy + sediment from rivers, cliffs, offshore. Throughputs: longshore drift, erosion, transport. Outputs: offshore loss, aeolian transport, human extraction. UK Atlantic coast experiences fetch > 5000 km producing high-energy waves.

Constructive waves (low frequency 6-8/min, height < 1 m) build beach with swash exceeding backwash. Destructive waves (high frequency 12-14/min, height > 1 m) erode and remove sediment offshore. UK coasts experience seasonal cycle: summer constructive, winter destructive.

Cell 2 from Flamborough Head to The Wash includes Holderness. Net southward drift transports cliff sediment to Spurn Head spit. Most cells operate as closed systems on annual timescales; longer-term offshore loss makes them semi-open.

Why do some rivers form deltas and others form estuaries?
options: Deltas form on big rivers and estuaries on small ones.
Deltas form where rivers deposit sediment faster than the sea can remove it (calm seas, heavy load); estuaries form where tidal energy removes sediment (strong tides).
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.

mcqs.q: What are the three cells of global atmospheric circulation?
options: Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
There is one big Hadley cell from the equator to each pole.
The Hadley cell (equator to 30 degrees), Ferrel cell (30 to 60 degrees) and Polar cell (60 degrees to poles) together redistribute heat from equator to poles.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.
Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
